headline: GOLD, SILVER IN TIGHT RANGE AT $4,165/$57 — ALL EYES ON OCT 28 FED RATE DECISION
snippet: Gold is holding a narrow range around $4,165/oz and silver near $57 as precious metals traders stay sidelined ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 policy meeting, where futures are pricing a roughly 22% chance of a rate hike. Global gold ETF holdings reached a record 4,256 tonnes in September — adding structural support — but the combination of elevated Treasury yields and an unresolved rate outlook is capping near-term upside; a hawkish hold or a hike could expose $4,075-$4,100 support for gold and $55.50 for silver, while a pause would re-open the $4,200-$4,300 target range.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM PRICE HITS $97/LB — 18-YEAR HIGH DRIVEN BY AI DATA CENTERS AND GRID DEMAND
snippet: The long-term U3O8 price reached $97 per pound as of end-September 2026 — the highest in 18 years and 13% above September 2025 levels — as surging electricity demand from AI data centers and industrial electrification drives utilities to lock in multi-year uranium supply at record contract prices. Industrial Info Resources tracks 101 uranium mining projects in the US with a total investment value of $8.62 billion, and the sustained long-term price premium over the spot price ($89.63) signals utilities are securing supply well in advance of anticipated reactor restarts and new builds.

headline: AURA ENERGY TIRIS URANIUM BFS: $500.3M POST-TAX NPV, $32.53/LB C1 COST, FID DECEMBER 2026
snippet: Aura Energy's (ASX: AEE) bankable feasibility study for the Tiris uranium project in Mauritania delivers a post-tax NPV of US$500.3M at US$90/lb U3O8 (28% IRR, 3.2-year payback), with development capex of US$349.8M and industry-leading C1 cash costs of US$32.53/lb and AISC of US$41.25/lb over a 26-year mine life averaging 1.8Mlb/yr. Aura is targeting a Final Investment Decision in December 2026 with first production by end-2028; an investor webinar presenting the study is scheduled for today, October 19 — note that 33% of the production schedule relies on Inferred resources and the US$350M project financing is not yet committed.

headline: DONE DEAL: EXIRO NICKEL CLOSES VALE THOMPSON ACQUISITION — CANADA GROWTH FUND CONSORTIUM TAKES HISTORIC MANITOBA MINE
snippet: Exiro Nickel Company completed its acquisition of Vale Base Metals' Thompson Mine Complex in Manitoba on October 16, with a consortium including Orion Resource Partners and the Canada Growth Fund holding 81.1% of Exiro while Vale retains 18.9% plus a multi-year offtake agreement for nickel concentrate. The US$200M investment package closed ahead of the original year-end target; Thompson produced 12,000 metric tonnes of finished nickel in 2025 (up 21% year-over-year) and Exiro plans to invest in restoring the mine toward prior peak output levels — making it one of the few Canadian nickel operations expanding rather than contracting in the post-2023 battery-metals downturn.

headline: BRUNSWICK EXPLORATION DRILLS 302-METRE SPODUMENE INTERCEPT AT ANATACAU MAIN — HOLE ENDS IN MINERALIZATION
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (TSX-V: BRW) reported drill hole AN-26-17 at its Anatacau Main project in Quebec's James Bay region returned 302 metres of spodumene-bearing pegmatite (estimated ~30% spodumene by volume; assays pending), extending the Anais dyke to 500m vertical depth and sitting 100m below hole AN-26-15, which returned 1.31% Li₂O over 202m — the hole was stopped by the rig's depth limit while still in mineralization. In a market where lithium carbonate prices just hit 10-month lows, this result is a reminder that low-cost, high-grade Quebec pegmatite deposits remain strategically valuable: the long-term supply outlook for battery-grade lithium favours projects with simple mineralogy and low strip ratios in stable jurisdictions.

headline: FLYNN GOLD HITS 12.95M AT 2.24G/T GOLD PLUS TUNGSTEN AT FIRETOWER — CRITICAL MINERALS TWIST ON TASMANIA PROJECT
snippet: Flynn Gold (ASX: FG1) reported hole FTDD001 at the Firetower project in Tasmania returned 12.95m at 2.24 g/t gold, 0.46% WO₃, 0.18% copper, 0.23% cobalt and 7.22 g/t silver — a polymetallic intersection where the tungsten (WO₃) content could add material value given that tungsten is a US-designated critical mineral with limited Western supply. The multi-element nature of the Firetower system distinguishes it from single-commodity exploration plays, and the cobalt-copper-gold-tungsten signature in Tasmania's geological setting warrants watching as the company advances toward a maiden resource.

headline: RECORD GOLD PRICE NOT REACHING BOTTOM LINE: AISC SURGING 16–23% IN 2026 AS ROYALTIES BITE
snippet: A detailed analysis of 2026 all-in sustaining cost trends finds gold producer AISC rising 16–23% year-over-year — driven by royalty increases triggered by gold's record price level (Ghana raised royalty rates in March 2026), fuel, and labour — creating a $1,500–$1,847/oz cost plateau that limits margin leverage even at $4,165 spot gold. For retail investors evaluating gold equity exposure, the key distinction to draw is between royalty streamers and low-royalty-jurisdiction producers (Nevada, Australia) versus high-royalty/high-inflation operators in West Africa and parts of Latin America, where the cost curve has structurally shifted and margin expansion is significantly more limited.

headline: GOLD PRICE FORECAST OCTOBER 2026: $4,500 BULL CASE RESTS ON FED PAUSE — $4,075 TEST IF YIELDS SURGE
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's October gold outlook puts a year-end base case in the $4,100–$4,300 range, with a bull scenario toward $4,500 if US-China trade tensions escalate or the Fed commits to a pause cycle, and a bear scenario toward $4,075 if the October FOMC meeting delivers a hawkish surprise or Treasury yields maintain their recent surge. With global gold ETF holdings at record levels and central bank demand near 720 tonnes expected for full-year 2026, the structural bid is strong — but the near-term directional call for mining equity investors hinges on whether next week's Fed statement shifts the rate-hike probability curve lower.

headline: US PROJECT VAULT READIES $1B CRITICAL MINERALS LOAN BLITZ — 101 US MINING PROJECTS WORTH $8.6B IN PIPELINE
snippet: The US government's Project Vault critical minerals reserve program is preparing up to $1 billion in loan facilities for American critical minerals manufacturers, targeting the 101 domestic uranium, rare earth, and battery metals projects in the construction and advanced-development pipeline. The loan program complements Vault's offtake strategy — which already includes Traxys's 850 t/yr NdPr deal with Arafura and similar agreements — and signals Washington's intent to provide demand-side certainty alongside capital access for projects that would otherwise struggle to secure commercial financing in a market still digesting the 2024–2026 commodity cycle corrections.
